sources.citation: Meek, Charles Kingsley. 1931. A Sudanese Kingdom: an ethnographical study of the Jukun-speaking peoples of Nigeria. London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner. xxxiii+548 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. I (pp. 3-15) discusses only Wukari Jukun (= Wapan): p. 14 'In the Wukari dialect tones are significant, i.e. homonyms are distinguished by differences in tone'; no stress/accent statement anywhere (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent: 'stress'/'accent' only in non-linguistic senses). Abinsi (= Wannu) appears only as wordlist 'II Abinsi Dialect' in the Appendix from p. 505, with no prosodic commentary. Silent on stress for Wannu.
